ei.subject: 수능특강Light 영어
ei.title: Shift in the Work-Time Paradigm Brought About by Industrialization

fullPassage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age (A)[changed / preserved] the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization (B)[raised / lowered] the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to (C)[reorganize / abandon] around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① changed - raised - reorganize: 산업화가 시간·노동·자본 관계를 '바꾸었고', 노동 시간당 가치를 '올렸으며', 사회가 생산성 원리로 '재편되기' 시작했다는 원문 내용.
❌ ② preserved - raised - reorganize: '보존했다'는 관계가 바뀌었다는 원문과 모순.
❌ ③ changed - lowered - reorganize: '낮췄다'는 산업화가 노동 가치를 끌어올렸다는 흐름과 반대.
❌ ④ changed - raised - abandon: '포기하다'는 사회가 새 원리로 '재편'되었다는 것과 모순.
det.tip: change(바꾸다) ↔ preserve(보존하다). raise(올리다) ↔ lower(낮추다). reorganize(재편하다) ↔ abandon(포기하다)

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with (A)[greater / lesser] speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is (B)[divided / united] into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became (C)[tied / opposed] to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ greater - divided - tied: 공장이 '더 큰' 속도와 규모로 생산하고, 근무일이 8시간씩 '나뉘며', 임금이 노력·생산에 '연결되었다'는 원문.
❌ ① lesser - divided - tied: '더 적은'은 생산성 증가와 모순.
❌ ② greater - united - tied: '하나로 합쳐지다'는 교대조로 '나뉜다'는 것과 반대.
❌ ④ greater - divided - opposed: '반대되는'은 임금과 노력이 '연결'되었다는 원문과 반대.
det.tip: greater(더 큰) ↔ lesser(더 적은). divide(나누다) ↔ unite(합치다). be tied to(~에 연결되다) ↔ be opposed to(~에 반대되다)

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce (A)[more / fewer] widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the (B)[potential / limited] value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became (C)[clock-oriented / nature-oriented], and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② more - potential - clock-oriented: 12시간 기계가 8시간 기계보다 '더 많은' 위젯을 생산하고, 산업화가 모든 근무 시간의 '잠재' 가치를 끌어올리며, 노동이 '시계 중심'으로 변했다는 원문.
❌ ① fewer - potential - clock-oriented: '더 적은'은 기계 가동 시간과 생산량의 비례 관계와 반대.
❌ ③ more - limited - clock-oriented: '제한된'은 원문 potential(잠재)과 의미가 다름.
❌ ④ more - potential - nature-oriented: '자연 중심'은 이전(harvest cycles)의 특징이지, 산업화 이후의 변화와 반대.
det.tip: more(더 많은) ↔ fewer(더 적은). potential(잠재적) vs limited(제한된). clock-oriented(시계 중심) vs nature-oriented(자연 중심)

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age ①<u>changed</u> the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is ②<u>divided</u> into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization ③<u>lowered</u> the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to ④<u>reorganize</u> around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① changed: 산업화가 관계를 '바꾸었다'는 원문 그대로.
❌ ② divided: 근무일이 8시간 교대로 '나뉜다'는 원문 그대로.
✅ ③ lowered: 원문은 raised(끌어올렸다). 일한 시간이 많을수록 돈을 더 많이 벌었다는 흐름과 정반대.
❌ ④ reorganize: 사회가 생산성 원리로 '재편'되기 시작했다는 원문 그대로.
det.tip: raise(끌어올리다) ↔ lower(낮추다). 더 오래 일할수록 보상이 커지는 구조 = 시간 가치 상승.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with ①<u>greater</u> speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce ②<u>fewer</u> widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines ③<u>humming</u>. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became ④<u>tied</u> to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① greater: '더 큰' 속도와 규모 — 원문 그대로.
✅ ② fewer: 원문은 more(더 많은). 12시간 기계가 8시간 기계보다 '더 적은' 위젯을 생산한다는 건 이후의 '24시간 기계가 가장 많이 생산한다'와 모순.
❌ ③ humming: 기계가 '계속 작동하는' 것 — 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ tied: 임금이 노력·생산에 '연결되었다' — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: 오래 돌수록 많이 생산 → more가 맞음. fewer는 정반대.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you ①<u>produced</u>, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to ②<u>effort</u> and production. Labor, previously ③<u>guided</u> by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around ④<u>old</u> principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① produced: 더 많은 위젯을 '생산했다' — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② effort: 임금이 '노력'과 생산에 연결된다 — 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ guided: 노동이 수확 주기에 의해 '이끌렸다' — 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ old: 원문은 new(새로운). 사회가 '오래된' 생산성 원리로 재편된다는 건 산업화 이후 '새로운' 패러다임이라는 흐름과 정반대.
det.tip: 산업화 = 새로운(new) 원리. 이전 시대 = 수확 주기(오래된 방식).

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and __________ than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ volume: 공장이 '더 큰 속도와 양'으로 생산할 수 있게 됨. 생산량과 속도가 함께 언급되는 맥락.
❌ ① silence: '침묵'은 생산 증가 맥락과 무관.
❌ ② danger: '위험'은 생산성 증가와 어울리지 않음.
❌ ③ confusion: '혼란'은 효율성 증대 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: speed(속도) + volume(양/규모) = 공장 생산성의 두 축.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour __________, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① shifts: 하루를 8시간씩 '교대조'로 나눈다는 것은 공장 근무 체계의 핵심. 기계를 계속 돌리기 위한 장치.
❌ ② meals: '식사'는 근무일 분할 맥락과 무관.
❌ ③ breaks: '휴식'은 기계를 계속 돌리려는 목적과 부합하지 않음.
❌ ④ prayers: '기도'는 공장 운영 맥락과 전혀 무관.
det.tip: eight-hour shifts = 8시간 교대근무. 공장이 24시간 돌아가려면 3교대가 필요.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by __________, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ harvest cycles: 산업화 이전 노동은 '수확 주기'에 맞춰졌음. 농경 사회 노동의 특징. 산업화 이후 '시계 중심'과 대비되는 표현.
❌ ① factory owners: '공장주'는 산업화 이후 등장한 개념이라 '이전 노동'과 시점이 맞지 않음.
❌ ② machine speed: '기계 속도'는 산업화 이후의 기준이지 이전 기준 아님.
❌ ④ wage contracts: '임금 계약'은 산업화 이후 개념.
det.tip: previously(이전에) = 산업화 이전 = 농업 = harvest cycles(수확 주기). 산업화 이후 = clock(시계).

Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is <u>divided</u> into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>divided</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② split: '쪼개다, 나누다'로 근무일을 8시간씩 '나누다'의 의미와 동일.
❌ ① combined: '합쳐진'은 divided의 반대.
❌ ③ stretched: '늘어진'은 분할이 아닌 연장.
❌ ④ hidden: '숨겨진'은 분할과 전혀 무관.
det.tip: divide(나누다) = split, separate. ↔ combine(합치다), unite(하나로 만들다)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>raised</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② increased: '증가시켰다'로 근무 시간의 가치를 '끌어올렸다'는 의미와 일치.
❌ ① dropped: '떨어뜨렸다'는 raised의 반의어.
❌ ③ ignored: '무시했다'는 가치를 올린 것과 무관.
❌ ④ hid: '숨겼다'는 맥락과 전혀 맞지 않음.
det.tip: raise(올리다, 끌어올리다) = increase, elevate, boost. ↔ drop, lower

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>potential</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ possible: '가능한'으로 '실현 가능한 잠재 가치'의 의미와 부합.
❌ ① actual: '실제의'는 potential(잠재적)과 대비되는 개념.
❌ ② fixed: '고정된'은 잠재력의 속성과 맞지 않음.
❌ ③ useless: '쓸모없는'은 가치를 올린 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: potential(잠재적) = possible, latent. 아직 실현되지 않은 가능성.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>greater</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① lesser: '더 적은, 더 작은'은 greater의 직접적 반의어.
❌ ② larger: '더 큰'은 greater의 동의어.
❌ ③ stronger: '더 강한'은 greater의 유사어.
❌ ④ higher: '더 높은'은 greater와 비슷한 방향.
det.tip: greater(더 큰) ↔ lesser, smaller(더 적은/작은). 동의어: larger, bigger.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>tied</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ detached: '분리된, 떨어진'은 tied(연결된)의 반의어.
❌ ① linked: '연결된'은 tied의 동의어.
❌ ② bound: '묶인'은 tied의 유사어.
❌ ④ connected: '연결된'은 tied의 동의어.
det.tip: tied(연결된, 묶인) ↔ detached, separated(분리된). 동의어: linked, bound, connected.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 없이 제시된 (A)와 (B)의 produce의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 생산하다 - (B) 꺼내 보이다: (A)에서는 공장이 제품을 '생산'하고, (B)에서는 여권을 '꺼내 보여준다'는 의미.
❌ ① (A) 꺼내 보이다 - (B) 생산하다: (A) 공장이 물건을 꺼내 보인다는 건 부자연스럽고, (B) 인터뷰어가 여권을 생산하는 것도 말이 안 됨.
❌ ③ (A) 생산하다 - (B) 생산하다: (B)에서 여권을 '생산한다'는 건 상식적으로 불가능.
❌ ④ (A) 꺼내 보이다 - (B) 꺼내 보이다: (A) 공장이 꺼내 보이는 것은 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: produce: 1. 생산하다(manufacture) - 공장에서 제품을 만들다. 2. 꺼내 보이다(show, present) - 문서 등을 제시하다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"The rate at which goods are produced or work is completed, especially in relation to the time and resources used."

det.analysis:
✅ ① productivity: 사용된 시간·자원 대비 재화가 생산되거나 일이 완료되는 비율 = 생산성.
❌ ② silence: '침묵'은 생산성과 무관.
❌ ③ harvest: '수확'은 농경 활동의 한 단계일 뿐.
❌ ④ confusion: '혼란'은 효율성의 반대 개념.
det.tip: productivity = 생산성. product(생산물) + -ivity(성질) = 얼마나 효율적으로 생산하는가.

questions.passage: Factories produced goods faster than ever before. The __________ (produce) of widgets rose sharply after industrialization.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: produce(동사: 생산하다) -> production(명사: 생산). 정관사 The 뒤 명사가 필요하며 '위젯의 생산'이라는 의미.
det.tip: produce(생산하다, 동사) -> production(생산, 명사) -> productive(생산적인, 형용사) -> productivity(생산성, 명사)

questions.passage: Industrialization changed how people worked. The __________ (industrial) of society reshaped daily life and work patterns.

det.analysis: industrial(형용사: 산업의) -> industrialization(명사: 산업화). 정관사 The 뒤에 동작/과정을 나타내는 명사가 필요.
det.tip: industry(산업, 명사) -> industrial(산업의, 형용사) -> industrialize(산업화하다, 동사) -> industrialization(산업화, 명사)

det.analysis:

det.analysis:
✅ ④ effort and production: 더 많이 일하고 더 많이 생산할수록 돈을 더 많이 벌었다는 흐름 → 임금이 '노력과 생산'에 연결됨.
